'''Michael Alan Rice''' (born March 4, 1955) is an American professor of fisheries and aquaculture at the [[University of Rhode Island]] and former state representative from [[South Kingstown, Rhode Island]].  A [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democrat]], he served in the [[Rhode Island House of Representatives]], representing the 35th district, encompassing the village of [[Kingston, Rhode Island|Kingston]] and West Kingston, and parts of the neighborhoods of Tuckertown, [[Wakefield, Rhode Island|Wakefield]] and [[Peace Dale, Rhode Island|Peace Dale]]. Rice was first elected on November 4, 2008, and served from January 3, 2009, to January 3, 2011.

==Education and early career==
Rice was born in [[San Jose, California]], to Richard Eugene Rice and Marilyn Joyce (Cardoza) Rice. He is a descendant of [[Portuguese Historical Museum|19th-century Azorean settlers in California]], thus being of [[Portuguese people|Portuguese]] descent, and a direct patrilineal descendant of New England colonist [[Edmund Rice (1638)|Edmund Rice]].<ref>Ancestry.com. California Birth Index, 1905-1995 [database on-line]. Provo, UT, USA: Ancestry.com Operations Inc, 2005.</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= http://webserver.rilin.state.ri.us/Journals10/HouseJournals10/Hjournal6-08.pdf |title= RI House Portuguese Caucus|publisher= RI House of Representatives Journal Volume 137, No. 57. p.91|date=8 June 2010|accessdate=15 Feb 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= http://www.edmund-rice.org/newsletters/vol_91_1_2017_winter.pdf|title= Nathaniel N. Rice|publisher= Edmund Rice (1638) Association Newsletter 91(1):9-18.|accessdate=15 Feb 2018}}</ref>

Michael Rice earned the rank of [[List of Eagle Scouts (Boy Scouts of America)|Eagle Scout]] in 1972 in [[Garden Grove, California]]. Rice attended [[Servite High School]] in [[Anaheim, California]] before attending the [[University of San Francisco]], and graduating with a B.S. in biology in 1977.<ref name=RI-SOS>{{cite web|url=https://opengov.sos.ri.gov/GOVDirectoryPublic/ViewGOVDirectoryDetails?RelationID=333&EntityID=1489&page=DetailLeg|title= Michael A. Rice Legislative Biography|publisher=Rhode Island Secretary of State|accessdate=March 22, 2012}}</ref><ref name =URI>{{cite web|url=https://webarchives.apps.uri.edu/special_collections/registers/manuscripts/msg240.xml |title= Guide to the Michael Rice Papers 1984-2014|publisher= University of Rhode Island Special Collections|accessdate=15 Feb 2018}}</ref> While working in the laboratory of physiologist [[Grover C. Stephens]] at the [[University of California, Irvine]], he earned both a master's degree in biology in 1981 and a PhD. in [[comparative physiology]] in 1987.

Rice served in the U.S. [[Peace Corps]] in the [[Philippines]] from 1981 to 1985 working with the [[Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources (Philippines)|Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources]].<ref name=Rice /><ref name=URI /> During that time, he worked to improve the sanitary quality of farmed oysters.<ref>Rosario, W.M., N. Poquiz and M.A. Rice. (1982). Oyster depuration: one answer to polluted estuaries. International Center for Living Aquatic Resources Management (Manila) Newsletter 5(3):14. [http://agris.fao.org/agris-search/search/display.do?f=1983/v903/XB8310145.xml;XB8310145 FAO Agris Depository]</ref><ref>Rice, M.A. (1992). {{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120728220306/http://openagricola.nal.usda.gov/Record/IND92046690|title="Bivalve aquaculture in warm tropical and sub-tropical waters with reference to sanitary water quality monitoring and postharvest disinfection"}}, ''Tropical Science'' 32:179-202.</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://punch.dagupan.com/articles/news/2018/11/legacy-on-footprints/ |title= Legacy on Footprints|publisher= Dagupan Sunday Punch, Dagupan, City, Philippines|author=Willie Lomibao|date=26 Nov 2018| accessdate= 30 Nov 2018}}</ref> In 1982, while working with José Maria DeGuzman of Value Trading Company Inc. in [[Dagupan]], he helped establish the first commercially successful farm for [[Serranidae|serranid grouper]] fish in the Philippines.<ref>Rice, M.A. and A.Z. DeVera. (1998). Aquaculture in Dagupan City, Philippines. World Aquaculture 29(1):18-24. [http://works.bepress.com/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1013&context=michael_rice Web Access]</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bcfishmonger.com/fishmongers_seafood_guide/2011/05/new-england-style-crab-cake-at-university-of-rhode-island.html|title=Crab Cakes at the University of Rhode Island|publisher=www.bcfishmonger.com|accessdate=March 28, 2013|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120628044129/http://www.bcfishmonger.com/fishmongers_seafood_guide/2011/05/new-england-style-crab-cake-at-university-of-rhode-island.html|archivedate=June 28, 2012}}</ref>

==Academic career==

Rice has spent most of his career in academia, first appointed to the faculty of the [[University of Rhode Island]] (URI) in October 1987.<ref>[http://www.uri.edu/catalog/catalogpdf/pdfs/17all.pdf  p. 318 in University of Rhode island General Catalog 2011-2012] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120722024212/http://www.uri.edu/catalog/catalogpdf/pdfs/17all.pdf |date=July 22, 2012 }}</ref>  His academic research interests are in the area of [[environmental physiology]] and [[ecology]] of [[bivalve molluscs]],<ref>Rice, M.A. (2007).  Bivalvia. pp. 141-44 In: Vol. 3, McGraw-Hill Encyclopedia of Science and Technology, 10th Edition. McGraw-Hill, New York.<!-- ISSN/ISBN needed --> [http://www.accessscience.com/content/bivalvia/085800 Web Access]</ref> and he has further research interests in the field of [[aquaculture]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://web.uri.edu/favs/michael-a-rice|title=University of Rhode Island: Michael A. Rice biography|accessdate=November 7, 2014}}</ref> His major contributions have been the demonstration that bivalve mollusks have the ability to absorb [[amino acids]] directly from seawater as a nutrition source, and that bivalves serve an important role in mediating the [[Nitrogen cycle#Marine nitrogen cycle|cycling of nitrogen]] and other nutrients within [[marine ecosystems]]. Additionally, he has studied the effects of shellfishing on the [[population ecology]] of bivalves. His research has led to refinements to the practice of managing shellfishery resources in coastal waters, [[estuary|estuaries]] and [[marine protected areas]].<ref>Rice, M.A., A. Valliere, and A. Caporelli. (2000). [http://works.bepress.com/michael_rice/26 A review of shellfish restoration and management projects in Rhode Island.], ''Journal of Shellfish Research'' 19: 401-08.</ref>

Rice has made contributions the science of shellfishery management and to the growth of the aquaculture industry in [[Rhode Island]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nrac.umd.edu/files/Factsheets/NRAC-110-2007_Rhode%20Island.pdf|title=Rhode Island Aquaculture Situation & Outlook Report|accessdate=2009-03-31|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110720090222/http://www.nrac.umd.edu/files/Factsheets/NRAC-110-2007_Rhode%20Island.pdf|archivedate=July 20, 2011}}</ref> and internationally,<ref>Rice, M. A. (2003). Aquaculture, pp. 372-417, in  B. Hazeltine and C. Bull (eds.), Field Guide to Appropriate Technology. Academic Press-Elsevier Science, New York. {{ISBN|0-12-335185-5}}</ref> including the [[Philippines]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://pbn.com/uri-philippine-fisheries-project-receives-25m-grant-largest-in-schools-history/|title=URI Philippine fisheries project receives $25M grant, largest in school's history|author=Emily Gowdy-Backus|publisher=[[Providence Business News]] |date=23 April 2018|accessdate=27 April 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://today.uri.edu/news/uri-professor-receives-prestigious-fisheries-award-from-philippine-government/|title=URI professor receives prestigious fisheries award from Philippine government|author=Todd McLeish|publisher=University of Rhode Island|date=10 Dec 2018|accessdate=24 Mar 2021}}</ref> [[Tanzania]],<ref>Rice, M.A., A. J. Mmochi, L. Zuberi and R.M. Savoie. (2006). Aquaculture in Tanzania.  World Aquaculture 37(4):50-57 [http://www.acdivoca.org/852571DC00681414/Lookup/WorldAquaculture/$file/WorldAquaculture.December06.pdf  PDF] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100215101558/http://www.acdivoca.org/852571DC00681414/Lookup/WorldAquaculture/$file/WorldAquaculture.December06.pdf |date=February 15, 2010 }}</ref> [[Georgia (country)|Georgia]], [[Indonesia]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.papuatimes.co.id/2019/05/09/university-rhode-of-island-gandeng-uncen-buka-fakultas-perikanan-dan-ilmu-kelautan/ |title= University of Rhode Island Gadeng UNCEN Buka Facultas Perikanan dan Ilmu Keluata|publisher= Papua Times|date=9 May 2019|accessdate=23 Sep 2019}}</ref> and [[Gambia|The Gambia]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ricentral.com/content/rice-studies-aquaculture-and-water-culture-gambia|title=Rice studies aquaculture and water in The Gambia|author= Brett Warnke|publisher=Narragansett Times|date= 27 Jan 2011|accessdate=8 July 2011|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://archive.today/20120912230459/http://www.ricentral.com/content/rice-studies-aquaculture-and-water-culture-gambia|archivedate=September 12, 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://thepoint.gm/africa/gambia/article/shoreline-water-quality-survey-gambias-water-relatively-clean|title=Shoreline Water Quality Survey: Gambia's water relatively clean|author=Abdou Rahman Sallah|publisher=The Point: Gambia|date=January 12, 2012|accessdate=January 15, 2012}}</ref> Working with Enrico Beridze of the Iberian Pontomarine Aquaculture Company, he introduced mussel farming to the [[Black Sea]] coast of Georgia.<ref>Rice, M.A. (2009). Aquaculture in the Republic of Georgia. World Aquaculture 40(1):26-29. [http://www.acdivoca.org/852571DC00681414/Lookup/Georgia-World%20Aquaculture2009/$file/Georgia-World%20Aquaculture2009.pdf PDF] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110719122907/http://www.acdivoca.org/852571DC00681414/Lookup/Georgia-World%20Aquaculture2009/$file/Georgia-World%20Aquaculture2009.pdf |date=July 19, 2011 }}</ref> He has led a study of [[Invasive species|invasive]] Australian crayfish in the [[Zambezi|Zambezi River]] watershed of [[Zambia]].<ref>{{cite journal|url= https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.2989/16085914.2024.2443944|title= The bio-invasion and population dynamics of ''Cherax quadricarinatus'' in Zambian waters| author= Nambeye E, Katapa C, Chimai-Mulenga B, Mudenda HG, & Rice MA|journal= African Journal of Aquatic Science|publisher= African Journal of Aquatic Science vol 50, no. 1, pp1-11 |date= 14 March 2025|volume= 50|issue= 1|pages= 88–98|doi= 10.2989/16085914.2024.2443944|bibcode= 2025AfJAS..50...88N|accessdate= 23 March 2025|doi-access= free}}</ref> Rice has been the recipient of three [[Fulbright Scholarship]] awards: Republic of the Philippines 1996–97;<ref>{{cite web|url=https://pbn.com/michael-a-rice2679/|title=Michael A. Rice|publisher=Providence Business News|author=Brian Gormley|date=27 Dec 1999|accessdate=30 Nov 2018}}</ref> [[Indonesia]] 1997; and Republic of the Philippines 2006.<ref name=URI />

At the University of Rhode Island he served as Chairman of the Department of Fisheries, Animal and Veterinary Science from 2000 to 2004, and again from 2025 to 2026.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://web.uri.edu/favs/people/|title= FAVS People|publisher= University of Rhode Island|date= July 2025|accessdate = 12 May 2026}}</ref><ref> University of Rhode Island General Catalog, 2025-26</ref>  Rice served as Chairman/President of the URI Faculty Senate from 2005 to 2007,<ref name=Rice/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.uri.edu/facsen/R05-06-4.html|title= Senate Resolution R05-06-4 in appreciation of Chairperson Rice|publisher=University of Rhode Island Faculty Senate|accessdate=May 31, 2012|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20100530155944/http://www.uri.edu/facsen/R05-06-4.html|archivedate=May 30, 2010}}</ref> and again from 2022 to 2023.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://drive.google.com/file/d/1sUSMdZYJXF6OjxtghXKEC2UxPD9HmyA8/view?usp=sharing|title= URI Faculty Senate Resolution Honoring outgoing President Rice|publisher= University of Rhode Island Faculty Senate|accessdate=31 May 2023}}</ref>  He subsequently served as the Grand Marshal of the 2023 Spring Commencement Ceremonies.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://web.uri.edu/commencement/wp-content/uploads/sites/1303/Commencement-Program_2023.pdf|title=2023 Commencement Program|publisher= University of Rhode Island|date=19 May 2023|accessdate=12 May 2026}}</ref>

==Civic involvement and politics==

Rice has served from 1999 to 2000 as the president of the [[Tavern Hall Preservation Society|Tavern Hall Club]], a not-for-profit  organization in [[Kingston, RI]] dedicated to the preservation of the historic (1738) Elisha Reynolds House as a community meeting place and social center.<ref name= Rice /><ref>''Tavern Hall Club and Preservation Society Presidents''. p.20. In: Tavern Hall Preservation Society 100th Anniversary. Tavern Hall Preservation Society, Kingston, RI 21pp.</ref>  He has also served as the President of the University Club of URI from 1995 to 1996.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.ourcampaigns.com/CandidateDetail.html?CandidateID=204829 | title=Candidate profile-Michael A. Rice | publisher=Our Campaigns|date= 12 Feb 2010|accessdate=4 Apr 2024}}</ref>  He was elected in 2007 to the board of directors and in 2008 as treasurer of the [[Edmund Rice (1638)]] Association, a [[Genealogy|genealogical]] and [[family history]] association that meets annually in [[Sudbury, Massachusetts]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.edmund-rice.org/ | title= Edmund Rice (1638) Association |accessdate= May 1, 2009}}</ref>  In 2011, Rice was nominated by [[Bruce Sundlun]] and appointed by [[Lincoln Chafee]] as a [[Rhode Island Commodore]].<ref name= Rice />

Prior to election to the Rhode Island House of Representatives in 2008, Rice served as an appointed member of a number of governmental commissions, including the Conservation Commission of [[South Kingstown, Rhode Island|South Kingstown]] from 1992 to 2008.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.southkingstownri.com/town-government/boards-commissions/35|title=South Kingstown Conservation Commission|accessdate=2009-06-05|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100418232847/http://www.southkingstownri.com/town-government/boards-commissions/35|archive-date=April 18, 2010|url-status=dead|df=mdy-all}}</ref> He chaired that commission from 1998 to 2008.<ref name= Rice />  Also prior to election, he was appointed by the Speaker of the RI House of Representatives, to the Legislative Commission on Aquaculture Development (1995–1998),<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rilin.state.ri.us/billtext97/housetext97/h6929.htm |title=1997H-6929 Aquaculture Commission |accessdate=2009-04-12 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120224180247/http://www.rilin.state.ri.us/billtext97/housetext97/h6929.htm |archivedate=February 24, 2012 }}</ref> to the Legislative Commission to Develop and Coordinate a Collaborative Effort to Formulate a Restoration Plan for the [[North Cape oil spill|''North Cape'']] Barge Oil Spill (1999),<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rilin.state.ri.us/billtext99/housetext99/h6460.htm |title=1999H-6460 Oil Spill Commission |accessdate=2009-04-12 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120224180250/http://www.rilin.state.ri.us/billtext99/housetext99/h6460.htm |archivedate=February 24, 2012 }}</ref> and as Legislative Commissioner proxy delegate to meetings of the [[Atlantic States Marine Fisheries Commission]] (1999–2000).<ref>Minutes of meetings of Atlantic States Marine Fisheries Commission, Atlantic Beach, NC (April, 1999); Portland, ME (June 2000); Portland, ME (October, 2000); and Atlantic City, NJ (December, 2000).  ASFMC, 1440 Eye St. NW Washington D.C. [http://www.asmfc.org  ASMFC].</ref>  Rice took an active advocacy role in developing recreational marine fishing licenses to gather fishery harvest data and to fund enhanced fishery management efforts within Rhode Island state waters.<ref>Rice, M.A. (2001). Not like California, RI’s free and open coastal fishing. Commentary January 4, 2001. [[The Providence Journal|Providence Journal Bulletin]].</ref>

In 2008, upon the decision of incumbent Rep. [[John P. Shanley Jr.|John Patrick Shanley]] (D-South Kingstown) not to run for a fifth term in the [[Rhode Island House of Representatives]], Rice ran and was challenged by Republican James K. Haldeman for the open seat. In the election held on November 4, 2008, Rice defeated Haldeman by 57.5% to 42.5%, carrying each of the district's five precincts.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ri.gov/election/results/2008/general_election/races/595.html# |title=Rhode Island Board of Elections: Representative in General Assembly District 35, 2008 general election |accessdate=2009-01-27}}</ref>

During the 2009 legislative session, Rice served on the House Committee on Separation of Powers and Government Oversight.  In the 2010 session, he served on the Committee on Environment and Natural Resources, and the House committees on Separation of Powers, Government Oversight, and Constituent Services, as well as the Special House Commission to Study the Structure and Workings of the Rhode Island Department of Transportation.<ref name= RI-SOS /><ref>{{cite web | url= http://webserver.rilin.state.ri.us/Journals09/HouseJournals09/HJournal1-07.pdf |title=Rhode Island House Journal 1-7-2009 | publisher= Rhode Island House of Representatives | accessdate= January 9, 2010}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url= http://webserver.rilin.state.ri.us/Journals10/HouseJournals10/HJournal1-05.pdf| title=Rhode Island House Journal 1-5-2010 | publisher= Rhode Island House of Representatives | accessdate= January 9, 2010}}</ref>

Rice was defeated for reelection by [[Spencer Dickinson (politician)|Spencer E. Dickinson]] in the September 14, 2010 Democratic Primary by a margin of 52.8-47.2%.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ri.gov/election/results/2010/statewide_primary/races/172.html |title=District 35 2010 Primary Results | publisher= Rhode Island Board of Elections | accessdate= Sep 15, 2010}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=http://blogs.wpri.com/2010/09/15/a-rough-night-for-ri-house-democratic-incumbents/ | title=A Rough Night for RI House Democratic Incumbents | publisher=WPRI.com | accessdate=Nov 20, 2011 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120502004904/http://blogs.wpri.com/2010/09/15/a-rough-night-for-ri-house-democratic-incumbents/ | archive-date=May 2, 2012 | url-status=dead }}</ref> He was targeted for defeat by the Rhode Island Labor Movement after voting against expansion of pension benefits for workers.<ref>{{cite web|last=Elk|first=Mike|title=Look to Rhode Island for How to Target Anti-Labor Democrats|url=https://www.huffpost.com/entry/look-to-rhode-island-for_b_734856|work=September 22, 2010|date=September 22, 2010 |publisher=Huffington Post|accessdate=4 Apr 2024}}</ref>

In 2011, Rice was appointed to the Rhode Island Democratic Party State Committee representing at-large [[Rhode Island's 2nd congressional district]], serving until 2017.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.ridemocrats.org/cms-assets/documents/142863-184938.2013statecommitteedocshare.pdf |title= 2013 RI Democratic State Committee Membership |publisher= RI Democratic State Committee| accessdate= 29 May 2014}}</ref> In 2013 he was appointed by [[Lincoln Chafee|Governor Chafee]] and received confirmation by the Rhode Island Senate to serve a two and a half-year partial term on the Rhode Island Marine Fisheries Council,<ref>{{cite web | url=http://webserver.rilin.state.ri.us/journals13/senatejournals13/sjournal6-11.pdf |title= p.14 Senate Journal 11 June 2013 |publisher= Rhode Island Senate| accessdate = 22 Jun 2013}}</ref> and reappointed to two terms by [[Gina Raimondo|Governor Raimondo]] ending on 1 April 2024.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://webserver.rilin.state.ri.us/Journals16/SenateJournals16/SJournal6-16.pdf |title= p.6 Senate Journal 16 June 2016 |publisher= Rhode Island Senate| accessdate = 4 Apr 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://dem.ri.gov/natural-resources-bureau/marine-fisheries/ri-marine-fisheries-council|title=Minutes of 1 April 2024 Meeting|publisher=Rhode Island Marine Fisheries Council|accessdate=2 April 2024}}</ref> He has been active with the [[American Association of University Professors]].<ref>{{cite web| url=https://uriaaup.org/about-us/committees/ | title=URI-AAUP Political Action Committee |accessdate=13 November 2022}}</ref>

==Selected legislation as enacted==

*'''2009-H5690a.''' ''An Act Relating to Agriculture and Forestry—Diseases and Parasites.'' This act established the [[Asian long-horned beetle]] and [[emerald ash borer]] beetles as nuisances. It also established penalties for unlawful importation and transportation of these invasive beetles and infested logs.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://webserver.rilin.state.ri.us/billtext09/housetext09/h5690a.pdf | title= 2009-H5690a | publisher = Rhode Island General Assembly | accessdate= 14 September 2014}}</ref>
*'''2009-H6226aa''' ''An Act Relating to Fish and Wildlife -- Recreational Saltwater Fishing License.'' This act created a recreational saltwater fishing license and made it unlawful to fish in the marine waters of the state without first obtaining a license. Funds derived from licenses are for enhancing recreational marine fisheries.<ref>{{cite web| url=http://webserver.rilin.state.ri.us/billtext09/housetext09/h6226aa.pdf |title=2009-H6226aa |publisher= Rhode Island General Assembly |accessdate=14 September 2014}}</ref>  The dedicated funds allowed for considerable expansion of the marine fisheries management and public programming by the Rhode Island Department of Environmental Management.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dem.ri.gov/programs/bnatres/marine/pdf/rlcrep18.pdf |title=Rhode Island Saltwater Recreational Fishing License Program Annual Report Fiscal Year 2018 - Prepared pursuant to RIGL §20-2.2-10 |publisher= Rhode Island Department of Environmental Management|date=1 Apr 2019|accessdate=11 Dec 2021}}</ref>
*'''2010-H7007''' ''An Act Relating to State Affairs and Government - Historian Laureate of Rhode Island.'' This act would establish the position of historian laureate in Rhode Island.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://webserver.rilegislature.gov/billtext10/housetext10/h7007.pdf|title=2010-H7007|publisher=Rhode Island General Assembly|date=6 Jan 2010|accessdate=11 May 2024}}</ref> Established RIGL §42-100.1-1 to §42-100.1-7 Historian Laureate of Rhode Island.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://webserver.rilegislature.gov//Statutes/TITLE42/42-100.1/INDEX.htm|title=RIGL §42-100.1|accessdate=11 May 2024}}</ref>
